name: v0.6.13
body:
The desktop app is updated too: [Desktop v0.0.7](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v0.0.7). This release is about the agent doing the work itself, working in your own browser, and safer defaults.

## The agent runs things itself

- **Commands run instead of instructions.** Asked to set something up, the agent runs the steps that need no input (for example `brew install …`) with your approval, and hands you only the steps that need you: a browser sign-in, a password, a yes/no. A command that waits for input is stopped quickly with "this step needs you", not left to time out.
- Long-running commands such as dev servers start in the background with readable output. Your usual toolchains (Homebrew, nvm, pyenv) are on the agent's PATH.
- `os.shell.run` accepts the command in the shapes models actually send, and a background job that ended with its turn is explained instead of polled again.

## Browser

- **Your own Chrome (opt-in).** Set `browser.connect` to `user-chrome` and the agent works in a tab of your signed-in Chrome. It sees only its own tabs, asks once per site before opening or reading it, and re-attaches after Chrome restarts. It has no access to cookies, passwords or storage, and password, code and card fields are masked.
- **Asks before it acts.** Submitting a form, paying, posting or typing a secret asks first, every time. `javascript:` addresses are refused. Scripting a browser through the shell is refused too; the agent uses its browser tool.
- **Screenshots** of a page, and a **compact page view** for small local models: only the interactive parts, and only what changed since the last step.

## Screen control on macOS (opt-in)

- With `tools.screen.enabled` the agent can take a screenshot, click and type in your apps. Browsers are look-only and terminals take clicks only, checked on every action.

## Safer by default

- **Project folders need your trust.** A folder's `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and project skills load only after you trust the folder, once per folder.
- Secrets are masked in tool output before the model reads them. Reading the agent's own secret files, and HTTP requests that send data, ask first.
- Every file of every installed skill is scanned.

## Local models

- On a GPU with its own memory the automatic context is held to 131,072 tokens and four slots, so big models stop spilling onto the CPU. Starting small and growing with the conversation is available as an option.
- A model that runs out of memory restarts once with half the window. A GPU build that crashes on load falls back to the CPU build.
- A reply cut at its length limit continues; local thinking models get room to finish.
- On Windows the agent waits for an old model server to free its port. On macOS older than the engine build supports, you get one plain sentence instead of a crash.
- Optional DRY anti-repeat sampling for llama.cpp engines.

## Agent

- One catalog of failure causes with a plain phrase and a next step.
- `os.fs.edit` tolerates whitespace, indentation and quote drift; a missing path suggests where the file actually is.
- An unknown tool name is an error the model can recover from, not a dead turn.
- Web search explains unreachable providers instead of waiting on each one.

## Also

- `verify.syntax` skips the Windows `python3` and `bash` stubs.
- The local server reads loopback addresses strictly and refuses a blank key.

name: Desktop v0.0.7
body:
Comes with the terminal agent [v0.6.13](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/v0.6.13).

## New

- **Files beside the chat.** Open the side panel any time (⌥⌘F) to see every file of this chat: files the agent made or mentioned, attachments, images and screenshots. Click one to preview text, code, Markdown, images, PDF and CSV.
- **Nicer replies.** Tables are real tables you can scroll and copy; steps, key-value pairs, comparisons, callouts and file cards get their own blocks.
- **Screenshots in the chat.** Screenshots the agent takes show up as images you can open, save or find.
- **Trust a folder once.** A folder with project instructions or skills asks once whether to trust them; change it later in Settings › Skills.
- **Import by project.** Claude Code chats are imported into one folder per project.

## Quieter

- Failed attempts the agent recovered from fold into one quiet line instead of red cards. Red is kept for what actually stopped the turn.
- One type scale across the app; small habits of the best apps: chat age in the sidebar, shortcut hints, one suggestion in an empty chat.

## Fixes

- The context popover no longer prints a 16-digit turn cap on cloud models.
- A model list printed before the agent exits is kept.

name: v0.6.12
body:
The desktop app is updated too: [Desktop v0.0.6](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v0.0.6). This release is about switching models without restarts, a doctor for your setup, remote use, and Linux packages.

## Linux packages

- **apt, dnf and AUR.** The terminal agent and the desktop app now ship as deb and rpm packages from our own signed repository, plus `atomic-agent-bin` and `atomic-agent-desktop-bin` on the AUR. Updates come with your system updates. Setup commands are in the [README](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent#linux-packages).
- `atomic-agent update` and `atomic-agent uninstall` notice a package install and tell you to use your package manager instead.

## Models

- **Live model switch.** Changing the model or the config over the local API no longer restarts the agent.
- **Known strong local models first.** Recommendations lead with well-known models that work with the agent.
- **Clear local errors.** A server answering 404, 405 or 400 is named, with a recheck. If the managed server or engine does not start, the reason is shown. An empty Ollama or LM Studio is called empty.
- **Context overflow** is compacted and retried with a plain message. The TUI suggests `/compact` or `/new` when context runs short.
- The memory model no longer starts on machines too weak for it.
- An unknown model id in `config.json` no longer crashes an older build on start.

## Doctor and data

- **`atag doctor`** checks the engine, port, model, memory, keys and connectivity, and fixes what it can.
- **Backup, restore, move and reset** of your data, with reset keeping downloaded models.

## Remote

- **Run the agent on one computer, use it from another.** The server on a network address now requires a key. The `/panel` page gives you chats, replies and approvals from your phone.

## Agent

- A loop detector stops repeated steps; a re-read after a failed edit counts as progress.
- Thinking models get their full reasoning budget. Grammar mode no longer emits empty commands.
- `os.shell.run` runs calls where the model put the command in `args` and left out `cmd`.
- The memory consolidator now picks candidates by age before the row cap, so it produces lessons again.
- Telegram tells you when another process holds the bot.
- Turn phases and a hint when the first reply is slow.

## Security

- Every installed skill is checked. Trace files are private to your account.

## Also

- Exa key in `/integrations`. Small TUI and CLI fixes.

name: Desktop v0.0.6
body:
Comes with terminal [v0.6.12](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/v0.6.12) inside.

## New

- **Switch models instantly.** Picking a model in the composer chip or in Settings › Models takes effect right away, without restarting the agent.
- **Straight to a chat on first run.** With no other model around, a small starter model downloads in the background while you can already type.
- **Folders for chats.** Create folders in the sidebar and drag chats into them. Imports keep the folders they came with.
- **A working folder per chat**, changed without restarting the agent or stopping a background task.
- **Doctor** in Settings › Diagnostics checks the engine, port, model, memory and keys, and fixes what it can.
- **Data:** backup, restore, move to another disk, and reset that keeps your models.
- **Connect to another computer** (Agent menu) by address and key, and use its models.
- **Read aloud** button on replies (macOS). **Keep running after the window closes** from the Agent menu.
- **Linux:** rpm next to the AppImage and deb, and apt, dnf and AUR packages.

## Faster and calmer

- Chats redraw without flicker and messages are cached. Code in replies is highlighted with a Copy button. Calmer animations.

## Fixes

- Set up a model opens Settings › Models › Local models.
- The engine installs even when Atomic Core already runs under another owner, and a failed install shows the real reason.
- Use in Settings › Models is fast. The Add a provider list opens under its button.
- The Connect window scrolls.
- Hardware acceleration turns off after repeated GPU crashes on Windows.

name: v0.6.11
body:
The desktop app is updated too: [Desktop v0.0.5](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v0.0.5). This release is mostly about approvals, safety and local models.

## Approvals

- **See the whole command.** A multi-line command is shown line by line in the approval, ending with `… +N more lines` when it does not fit. Shell arguments are quoted the way a shell reads them, so the preview is the command that will run.
- **Read past the preview.** In the TUI, `ctrl+z` (or "view full command") pages through the full command, then goes back to the short preview. In Telegram, a cut preview arrives with the full command as `full-command.txt` right before the approval message.
- **Allow in this chat:** the local API accepts `allow-in-chat`, so a client can approve the same program (for example `git`) for the rest of one chat. Other programs and other chats still ask, and nothing is saved.

## Security

- **Shell commands no longer see your API keys.** Commands the agent runs get its environment without variables named like keys, tokens, secrets or passwords. Name the ones a command still needs in `tools.shell.envPassthrough`.
- **MCP servers started from a command** get only basic system variables plus the `env` from their own config, not every provider key.
- **Telegram pairing** needs a 6-digit one-time code shown on your screen, valid for 5 minutes: send `/start <code>` to the bot. A paired owner is only replaced after you confirm. Desktop can now pair over the local API too.
- Web pages, search results, HTTP replies and MCP answers are marked as outside text in tool results, and fake chat-template tokens in them are removed.
- A project skill can no longer replace a global skill of the same name. On Windows, `config.json` is readable only by your account. Webhook secrets are compared in constant time.

## Local models

- **Thinking models get room to think.** Context compaction leaves space for the model's reasoning, so summaries stop failing on thinking models. The local reasoning budget defaults to no limit again (an old written 1500 is moved to 0).
- **Broken tool-call JSON is repaired** (trailing commas, single quotes, missing brackets) before the agent spends another step asking the model again.
- **Looping replies are cut off.** A reply cut at the output limit is retried once with a higher cap, or with the same cap and a note when the reply was repeating itself. On cloud models a long turn is retried instead of failing.
- **Full tool output is saved to a file** when a long result is clipped, so the model can read the part it needs instead of running the command again.
- **File changed since last read:** a write or edit warns the model when the file changed after it last read it, for example when you saved it in your editor.
- `os.fs.edit` matches text even when the model dropped a blank line or trailing spaces.
- **llama.cpp default port is now 9931**, matching current `llama-server`. Saved URLs are not changed, and the "not reachable" hint mentions both 9931 and 8080. A server answering 404 or 405 is reported as the wrong server or no model loaded.
- The embedding model keeps running when chat moves to a cloud model, and memory follows an embedding model change without a restart.

## Also new

- **`/enhance`** in the TUI rewrites a draft prompt and puts it back in the composer for you to edit. Nothing is sent until you press Enter.
- Streaming replies in the TUI are drawn as markdown as they arrive. Finished file cards have a `[copy path]` chip.
- The agent also reads project rules from `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `.cursor/rules`.
- MCP servers accept `enabledTools` and `disabledTools` to offer only some of their tools.
- `atomic-agent run` queues piped lines that arrive during a turn instead of dropping them. `atomic-agent uninstall` warns when the desktop app shares the same data folder.

## Fixes

- An expired `claude` or Codex login shows the CLI's own error and a sign-in hint instead of "no output".
- Local replies that quote a word are no longer cut off mid-sentence.
- `verify.syntax` checks JavaScript with a real Node in release builds.
- A provider without a chat model can no longer be picked as the chat model.

## Windows

- Russian and other non-English text shows correctly in the console: the CLI switches the console to UTF-8 for the session and restores it on exit.

name: Desktop v0.0.5
body:
The desktop app gets safer approvals, Telegram pairing in the app, a tidier chat and zoom, plus many fixes. It includes everything in Atomic Agent v0.6.11.

## Approvals

- **The card shows what you approve.** A multi-line command says "(+N more lines)" and opens its full preview from the start. The "Ran ..." line in the chat says the same.
- **Allow in this chat** approves the same program (for example `git`) for the rest of the chat. Other programs and other chats still ask, and nothing is saved.
- **Shell commands no longer see your API keys,** and MCP servers get only the keys in their own config.

## Chat

- **Finished turns fold into one summary line,** like "Used 4 tools · 12 s". Click it to see the steps. Settings › General can always show them.
- **Ask again** under the last reply of a turn that ran no tools. After a turn that changed files, a greyed icon explains why it is not offered.
- **Zoom:** Cmd+= and Cmd+- zoom in and out, Cmd+0 is Actual Size. The sidebar moves to Cmd+\ (Ctrl on Windows and Linux). Right-click on text opens an edit menu with spellcheck.
- **Tasks and Skills** have their own rows in the sidebar. A narrow window gets a drawer with the chat list.
- **New task in plain words:** describe what the agent should do and when, and it sets up the schedule in a new chat.
- **Command palette (Cmd+K)** finds things with typos and missing letters, such as "mdl" for Models.
- The model list in the composer shows every downloaded local model and every cloud provider with a working key.

## Studio

- **Improve prompt** rewrites your prompt with the chat model, with Undo.
- **Recent** lists your last 12 prompts on each page.
- Greyed-out modes say why they are off. A busy cloud model offers Retry or another model. The video gallery has Load more and a full Pinned tab.

## Setup and settings

- **Telegram pairing in the app:** Pair shows a 6-digit one-time code. Send `/start <code>` to your bot within 5 minutes. Every Telegram line that needs a restart has a **Restart agent** button, and the app stays open.
- **MCP smart add:** paste a server's command line, its URL or JSON.
- **Claude Code and Codex subscriptions** are in Add provider.
- **Memory model card** shows its own state: Starting, Running, Not running, Off or Not downloaded.
- **Too big for this Mac:** downloading or starting a model that needs more memory than the Mac has asks first and suggests one that fits.
- **Move to Applications:** a Mac app run from the disk image or Downloads offers to move itself, so updates keep working.
- **llama.cpp custom server** suggests port 9931, the default of current `llama-server`. Saved addresses are not changed.
- Diagnostics opens on health rows for engine, model and provider, each with one fix button.
- The chosen working folder is remembered across restarts, and running turns keep going when it changes.

## Fixes

- The agent restarts by itself if it stops unexpectedly, and the window reloads after a page crash.
- A local model that is not running says so and offers **Start model**. A model that could not load, or moved to the CPU build, says that instead of asking to download the engine again.
- A server that answers 404 or 405 is named as the wrong server. A rejected key shows "Key rejected" with Restart model.
- "Local model ready" appears in setup only after the model started.
- Thinking budget offers only values llama.cpp can hold, and thinking models get room to finish.
- The embedding model keeps running when chat switches to cloud.
- The uncensored model is labelled "Fewer refusals" with a plain explanation.

## Downloads

- macOS, Apple Silicon: `Atomic-Agent-0.0.5-arm64.dmg`
- Windows, x64: `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.5-x64.exe`
- Windows on ARM (Snapdragon): `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.5-arm64.exe`. Local models run on the CPU there.
- Linux, x64 and ARM64: `.AppImage` or `.deb`

name: v0.6.10
body:
The desktop app is updated too: [Desktop v0.0.4](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v0.0.4), with a new Studio for images and video.

## Images and video

- New `image.generate`: the agent draws pictures on OpenRouter through Atomic Chat Core and saves them in the working folder. Square, landscape, portrait or an exact aspect ratio, up to 4 pictures in one call.
- New `video.generate`: a 4, 6 or 8 second clip from a prompt, or from a picture as the first frame. 4 seconds is the default and the cheapest. The clip is saved as `video-<time>.mp4` and sent with the reply; Telegram plays it inline.
- Both tools appear once an OpenRouter key is set, and ask before they spend money (new approval category `paid_generation`). OpenRouter charges your account; stopping a clip does not cancel the charge.
- When a video model is busy, the agent tells you which one and offers up to three others. It does not switch to a pricier model on its own.
- Long tool calls report progress on the HTTP stream as `tool_update` frames.

## Also new

- **Web search** falls back to Exa's free endpoint when DuckDuckGo is unavailable. When Exa's free searches run out, the result says a key is needed (`key_required` on the `tool_result` frame) instead of failing silently.
- **Rename a chat:** `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with `{ title }`. A name you set is kept: auto-naming and a turn that was already running never put the old one back.
- **Archives:** the attachments hint names `os.fs.archive.list` and `os.fs.archive.extract`, so the agent opens zip, tar, gz and tgz files it receives.
- **Atomic Chat Core 0.18.6** (was 0.16.0). An existing install switches over on its next idle start.

name: Desktop v0.0.4
body:
The desktop app gets a Studio for making images and video, local or in the cloud, plus more than 50 fixes. It includes everything in Atomic Agent v0.6.10.

## Studio

A new Studio group in the sidebar, with Images and Video pages.

- **Images:** Create, Edit, Reference, Transform, Inpaint, Extend and Upscale, each one on when the chosen model supports it. Drop, paste or pick source, mask and reference pictures. Shapes, quality, count, and an Advanced fold for negative prompt, steps, guidance and seed. A viewer with Save as, Copy, Use as source, Restore these settings and Send to chat, and a library with Pinned.
- **Video:** from text or from a first frame, 4, 6 or 8 seconds (4 by default), resolution, 16:9 or 9:16, sound. A player and a clip library.
- **Cloud models** run on OpenRouter with your key. When OpenRouter publishes a price per image or per second, the Generate button shows it. OpenRouter charges your account, and Stop does not cancel a cloud charge.
- **Local models** come from the Atomic Chat catalog: the download resumes, is checked against its checksum and checks free disk space first. Non-commercial and 18+ models carry labels.
- **Your local chat model and Studio share the GPU.** A local picture pauses the local chat model and brings it back afterwards; a chat turn waits with a Stop link meanwhile.
- Files are kept in `models/studio/images` and `models/studio/videos` in the app's data folder, and survive engine updates.

The agent can make them too: ask for a picture or a clip in chat. Videos play inline, and pictures and clips have Open in Studio.

## Also new

- **Rename a chat** from its menu or with a double-click.
- **Attach archives:** zip, tar, gz and tgz.
- **Free disk space** is checked before a local model download.
- **Exa key card:** when web search runs out of free searches, the chat asks for a free Exa key right there. Settings › General has the same field.
- **Code blocks** get a header with the language and a Copy button.
- **Command palette** finds up to 20 chats, best match first.
- **Reasoning rows** show how long the model thought.
- **Atomic Chat Core 0.18.6** comes inside the installer.

## Fixes

- A provider that answers with an HTTP error says it refused, instead of "not answering". A failed model start shows a short reason with Details.
- Onboarding puts a model already on your computer first, links to each provider's key page, and points Ollama and LM Studio users to their apps.
- Telegram pairing copy matches what the app can do, asks before wiping the token or owner, and ignores double clicks.
- Clearer approval wording, context ring, Thinking budget, Diagnostics (with buttons to open the data folder, working folder and logs), MCP and embedding explanations.
- Fusion seats show full model names. A file dropped over Settings, the palette or a dialog is no longer attached to the chat.
- Higher contrast for secondary text (WCAG AA).

## Downloads

- macOS, Apple Silicon: `Atomic-Agent-0.0.4-arm64.dmg`
- Windows, x64: `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.4-x64.exe`
- Windows on ARM (Snapdragon): `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.4-arm64.exe`. Local models run on the CPU there.
- Linux, x64 and ARM64: `.AppImage` or `.deb`

name: v0.6.9
body:
The desktop app is updated too: [Desktop v0.0.3](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v0.0.3). From this release on, the terminal agent and the desktop app share one setup.

## One setup for the terminal and the desktop

- The desktop app now uses the terminal agent's folder, `~/.atomic-agent`. Chats, memory, skills, keys and settings are the same in both.
- Both can run at once. Quitting one no longer stops a local model the other is using.
- Scheduled tasks run once, in whichever app was started first. Telegram works the same way.
- Settings saved in one app no longer overwrite a change the other made a moment earlier. A save that would have lost it is refused and retried.
- New: `atomic-agent import atomic-desktop --source <dir>` brings chats, scheduled tasks and memory from an older desktop folder. The desktop app runs it for you on first start.

## Faster context compaction

- Compaction takes seconds. The agent keeps a running summary in the background, so it is ready when the context fills up, and a slow model no longer starts a chain of retries.
- A paused task is summarised from its own records if the summary step fails.

## Clearer failures

- A failed turn says what went wrong in plain words, with the raw error on a Details line, and offers [try again].
- Common provider HTTP statuses are put into words while the agent waits.
- The Fallback pane says which failure caused a switch to the fallback model.
- Fusion flags a worker that has run more than twice as long as expected.

## Tools

- New `os.fs.move` moves and renames files without the shell.
- `os.fs.grep` keeps the matches it found when ripgrep times out, and `os.fs.glob` stops a walk that takes too long.
- The Fusion planner can read the web (`os.web.fetch`, `os.web.search`). Reading a folder or a device such as `/dev/null` as a file now says what to do instead.
- Files the agent attaches to a reply reach HTTP clients that ask for them, not only Telegram and Discord.

## Local models

- Atomic Chat Core 0.16.0. An existing install keeps working and switches over on its next idle start. Memory search by meaning keeps working on Core 0.13.6.
- An embedding-only OpenAI-compatible provider no longer needs a chat model.
- The reasoning budget is capped at what llama.cpp grammars accept.

name: Desktop v0.0.3
body:
The desktop app now shares one setup with the terminal agent, and you can attach files and images to a message. It includes everything in Atomic Agent v0.6.9.

## One setup with the terminal

- The app now uses the same folder as the terminal agent, `~/.atomic-agent`. Chats, memory, skills, keys and settings are shared.
- **Already using the desktop?** On first start, your data from `~/.atomic-agent-desktop` comes over once:
  - a backup is made first;
  - where both apps have a setting, the terminal's wins;
  - local model files are moved, not downloaded again;
  - the old folder is kept;
  - a notice says what moved and where the backup is.
- **Set up in the terminal already?** The app opens straight to your chats with a short note, instead of the setup wizard.
- Both apps can be open at once. Quitting the desktop no longer stops a local model the terminal is using, and settings saved in one do not overwrite the other.

## Attachments and pictures

- Attach images and files with the + button, by dropping them on the window, or by pasting an image. They show as chips above the message box.
- Pictures the agent sends back appear right in the chat. Click one for a full-screen view with Save As and Show in Finder (Show in Explorer on Windows).

## Also new

- **Composio** can be set up from Settings › Connections.
- **Compaction** takes seconds. A manual Compact now can run past five minutes when it needs to.
- **Failed turns** show a short reason with the raw error under Details, and a Try again button. Provider HTTP statuses are put into words on the waiting strip.
- **Atomic Chat Core 0.16.0** comes inside the installer.
- **Look it up** honours your Hugging Face mirror setting.

## Downloads

- macOS, Apple Silicon: `Atomic-Agent-0.0.3-arm64.dmg`
- Windows, x64: `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.3-x64.exe`
- Windows on ARM (Snapdragon): `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.3-arm64.exe`. Local models run on the CPU there.
- Linux, x64 and ARM64: `.AppImage` or `.deb`

name: v0.6.8
body:
The desktop app is updated too: [Desktop v0.0.2](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/releases/tag/desktop-v0.0.2).

## Atomic Chat Core is the local engine

- Local models now run through Atomic Chat Core, the engine the Atomic Chat app uses. It downloads and manages llama.cpp for you. Existing setups move over on first start (config v77). Your model files are kept and nothing is downloaded again.
- The engine choice is no longer shown in the TUI. `atomic-agent models engine llama-server` switches back if you need to.
- Context size and GPU placement are fitted to your machine by Core.

## Memory search by meaning

- New embedding model: **EmbeddingGemma 2** from Google (310 MB, 100+ languages). Turn it on with `atomic-agent models pull-embedding embeddinggemma-2`, `models use-embedding embeddinggemma-2` and `models start-embedding`. It runs through Atomic Chat Core.
- Memory now finds notes by meaning, not only by shared words. A note in one language can be found by a question in another.
- Notes written before you turned embeddings on, or before you switched models, are re-embedded in the background after start. `atomic-agent memory reindex` does it by hand.
- Fixed: semantic search turned itself off after 200 notes, and keyword ranking in hybrid search was inverted.
- `memory.embeddings.fts5Weight`, `vectorWeight` and `bruteForceCeiling` in `config.json` now take effect.
- Semantic search works while a local chat model is active. With a cloud chat model, memory uses keyword search for now.

## Projects and cloud models

- Cloud workspaces load the project's own instructions (`AGENTS.md`) and skills. Outside a git project only the folder root is read, with a size limit, so starting in your home folder no longer overflows the model.
- Cloud models keep the full conversation context, and provider policies are migrated.

## Local models

- Faster model switching.
- Add a GGUF you already have by its path: in the Local models panel press `a` and paste the file path. Nothing is copied or downloaded.
- An unusable `llama-server.key` is regenerated instead of running without a key.

## Fixes

- Piped command output is no longer cut at 64 KB. Lists such as `models search --json` arrive whole.
- A rate limit is no longer read as a billing problem, and a moderation refusal no longer as a bad API key.
- Fusion: a role's model is reset when its provider is removed or changed, so the old model no longer sticks.
- Finished turns show a one-line summary under their tool cards in the TUI.

name: Desktop v0.0.2
body:
This release runs local models through Atomic Chat Core, adds memory search by meaning, and tidies up the sidebar and settings. It includes everything in Atomic Agent v0.6.8.

## What's new

- **Atomic Chat Core** comes inside the installer, so the first start does not download an engine. If it can't start, a card explains why and offers Download again.
- **Memory by meaning:** pick EmbeddingGemma 2 under Settings › Models › Embedding models. Memory then finds notes by meaning and across languages, while a local chat model is active.
- **Sidebar:** search and collapse sit on one row next to the window buttons. Each chat has a "…" menu (also on right click) with Pin, Mark as read or unread, and Delete. Pinned chats get their own section.
- **Settings › Models:** cloud providers show their full live model list with a filter. The pane no longer jumps to the top while you scroll. DashScope (Qwen) is a ready preset.
- **Context:** `/compact` and Compact now in the context popover show their progress and the token count before and after.
- **Quitting** no longer hangs while the model server stops.

## Fixes

- Mark as unread shows the blue dot. Before, chats that ever had a failed turn turned red.
- Menu items in the chat "…" menu light up on hover.
- Removing the EmbeddingGemma 2 model works while it is running.

## Downloads

- macOS, Apple Silicon: `Atomic-Agent-0.0.2-arm64.dmg`
- Windows, x64: `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.2-x64.exe`

name: v0.6.7
body:
## Context compaction

- New `/compact` command. It summarizes the older part of the conversation and the model reads that summary instead of the old messages. `/compact show` prints the saved summary.
- Compaction also runs on its own when the conversation fills 90% of the room the model window leaves for it, or when the oldest tasks are about to drop out of `agent.conversationMaxPairs`. It shrinks the history to about 65% of that room. Before, older messages were cut off.
- The full session transcript stays on disk unchanged. The opening request of the current task and your latest message are always kept word for word.
- The summary is written by the model the session already uses, with no tools. The TUI shows the status, the elapsed time and which part is being summarized, and Esc cancels it.
- If summarizing fails, the agent falls back to the old trimming and does not try again on its own until the next turn. If the provider refuses a request as too long for its window, the agent compacts and retries that request once.
- Settings live under `agent.compaction` in `config.json`: `auto`, `triggerRatio`, `targetRatio`, `summaryMaxTokens`, `timeoutMs` and `maxTotalTimeoutMs`. The whole operation has a 10-minute limit by default.
- Over HTTP: `POST /api/sessions/{id}/compact` and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/compaction`.

## Windows: local models on NVIDIA GPUs

- With an NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 12.4 or newer, the agent now picks the CUDA 12.4 engine build, which ships its own CUDA runtime. Before, it could pick the CUDA 13.3 build, which did not include the runtime, so on a PC without the CUDA Toolkit the model silently ran on the CPU.
- An existing install with that problem is replaced automatically the next time the local model starts, with no manual steps.
- RTX 50-series cards get the Vulkan build, since the CUDA 12.4 build has no code for them.
- If a CUDA download arrives without its runtime, the agent installs the Vulkan build of the same release instead and tries CUDA again only on a newer release.
- `cuda-13.3` is no longer picked automatically. You can still set it with `localModels.managed.backendVariant`, and it needs the CUDA Toolkit installed.

## Approvals

- When you decline a tool call, the model is told that you declined it, not "approval denied". The same call is not asked again in that turn.
- When the agent sends several calls that need approval in one step, it now waits for each approval and runs them, instead of keeping only one call.

## Memory

- Memory no longer stores names you never typed. Small local models used to copy an example name into your profile.
- One-off instructions such as "reply exactly OK" or "don't use tools" are no longer saved as lasting preferences. Short pings skip the memory step. Words like "remember", "always" or "from now on" still save what follows.
- The same profile fact is not written twice.

## Local models and Fusion

- The managed `llama-server` now starts with an API key, so a web page open in your browser cannot call it. The key is generated once and kept in `<models dir>/llama-server.key`, or taken from `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_API_KEY`. Scripts or other apps that call the managed server directly must send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A server started by an older version runs without a key until you restart it with `atomic-agent models stop` and `models start`.
- On Macs and other machines with unified memory, the automatic context size leaves the system at least 4 GiB or 25% of RAM, whichever is larger, and caps the KV cache at 1/16 of RAM.
- A large `localModels.completionMaxTokens` no longer squeezes the conversation to almost nothing. The reply reserve is capped at half the model window, and the context panel shows the reserve and free space the window allows.
- When the device probe fails, the managed server starts with a 32,768-token context instead of 16,384, which left no room for the prompt.
- A local server that is stuck on a request is detected as frozen. A failed `llama-server` start no longer crashes the agent.
- Each Fusion worker row in the TUI now shows how much context the worker holds, for example `12.3k ctx`.
- Local Fusion workers get time to read their brief, and their reply limit matches their time limit. A large `completionMaxTokens` no longer cuts the worker pool down to one worker.
- `models status` works on a fresh install, before the server has ever started.

## Providers and fallback

- An account that cannot pay (402, or a 403/429 that says funds, balance or billing) ends the turn with the provider's own message, instead of waiting five minutes on the last fallback.
- Provider errors now include what the provider said. A wrong Gemini key no longer shows only `rejected the request (400)`.
- When the main provider refuses its API key and the fallback chain runs out, the turn ends right away with the key's error instead of waiting for an outage to pass.
- A fallback provider with no API key is skipped and marked `no key, skipped` in the Fallback pane, instead of adding a certain 401 to every turn.
- A key with a non-ASCII character, or a missing key, now says what is wrong with it instead of `rejected the API key (401)`.
- A broken provider entry that is not active, such as one saved without a model, no longer stops the agent from starting.
- `/model` switches to a local server such as LM Studio or Ollama without asking for a key.
- Perplexity chat works. Every turn used to fail with 404.
- `models search --refresh` lists Gemini models and works with the Anthropic preset.
- AI/ML API offers `mistral-small-2603` in place of the retired `mistral-large-2512`.
- In the LLM tab, `d` on a cloud provider removes it after you confirm with `y`. The active provider cannot be removed, and the removed provider also leaves the fallback chain.

## Windows

- On Windows the agent is told that PowerShell cmdlets such as `New-Item` and `Move-Item` do not work in its `cmd.exe` shell, and is shown the `mkdir` and `move` forms to use instead.
- `os.fs.write` is described as making files only, so models stop creating empty files where they meant to make folders.
- `cmd.exe` gets each command line exactly as written.
- HTTPS requests no longer fail when the certificate revocation server cannot be reached.
- `atomic-agent.exe` is signed again. In v0.6.6 it shipped unsigned.

## Tasks, Telegram, web search

- `atomic-agent task create --at` now waits until that time. Before, the task ran on the next scheduler tick. `--at` takes Unix milliseconds or an ISO-8601 date or date-time, rejects anything else, and warns when the time is in the past.
- A scheduled task's run now stops when its agent stops, when you cancel it, or when the process that owns it exits.
- The Telegram bot keeps reconnecting after a dropped connection.
- Web search skips Exa when no Exa key is set, instead of calling its keyless tier.

## Replies and sessions

- When a reply has a link on the same site as a link from this turn's tool results but with a different path, the agent is asked once to copy the link exactly or drop it.
- Reading the same unchanged lines of a file again shows a pointer to the earlier read instead of a second copy.
- Chat titles no longer include a thinking model's reasoning.
- A turn left running by a crash or shutdown is marked as cancelled at the next start.
- TUI: one progress bar per download, and a thread stays whole when you switch away mid-answer.

## serve and HTTP API

- Idle streams on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/api/events` get a `: keepalive` comment every 15 seconds, so a turn waiting on an approval is no longer dropped by the client's timeout.
- `/api/events` no longer replays approval requests that were already cancelled.
- `serve` notices when a client disconnects and stops that turn.
- Each tool call's result is sent on the stream when it finishes. `/api/capabilities` lists only the tools the agent is offered.
- New routes: `GET` and `POST /api/coding-mode`, `POST /api/context-preview`, and the two compaction routes above. Session rows carry their title.
- `error` and `provider_waiting` frames name the billing cause and the providers that failed before. A stopped turn's `loop_failed` frame reads as cancelled.
- `serve` now writes its structured log.

## Config, privacy, security

- `config.json` is written readable by its owner only (0600). `atomic-agent config set - < config.json` reads the whole file from stdin, so an API key never has to go on the command line.
- `skill browse` and `skill search` read ClawHub and the GitHub taps together.
- A `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` is sent only to GitHub's own hosts. Before, any download URL that contained "github.com" could receive it.
- A subscription provider such as Claude Code no longer receives the agent's API keys in its environment, so the CLI uses your subscription instead of an API key it finds there.
- Analytics events and crash reports now say whether they came from the TUI, the command line or the desktop app, and the terminal and desktop app share one install id per machine. When you turn analytics off, one last event records that it was turned off. Crash reports name only the kind of host a failed connection went to (`localhost`, `private`, `known_cloud` or `other`), never the host.
- `ATOMIC_AGENT_ANALYTICS=off` turns off analytics and crash reports for that process, whatever the config says.
- User guides moved to `docs/user/` (`tui.md`, `memory.md`).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/compare/v0.6.6...v0.6.7

name: Desktop v0.0.1
body:
The first public build of the Atomic Agent desktop app. It runs the same agent as the terminal version, bundled inside, and gives it a chat window. You can download local models and run them on your machine, connect a cloud provider, or use Fusion. Tool calls show as cards in the chat, and approvals appear inline. Settings cover MCP servers, skills, memory, scheduled tasks and a Telegram bot, and you can import your history from Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw and others. On macOS 26 or later you can also dictate messages with Apple's on-device speech.

## Downloads

- macOS, Apple Silicon: `Atomic-Agent-0.0.1-arm64.dmg`
- Windows, x64: `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.1-x64.exe`
- Windows on ARM (Snapdragon): `Atomic-Agent-Setup-0.0.1-arm64.exe`. Local models run on the CPU there.
- Linux, x64 and ARM64: `.AppImage` or `.deb`

## Good to know

- The app checks for new versions shortly after it opens and then every 6 hours, and asks before downloading or installing anything. Turn this off with "Check for updates automatically" in Settings › General. On macOS, move the app to Applications first, because an app run from the disk image or Downloads cannot update itself. On Linux there are no in-app updates yet, so take new versions from this page.
- macOS needs version 14 or later.
- Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
- The macOS and Windows builds are signed. The Linux builds are not.
- The desktop app keeps its own settings, API keys, sessions and memory in `~/.atomic-agent-desktop`, separate from the terminal agent's `~/.atomic-agent`. Setting up the app does not change your terminal setup.
- Anonymous usage analytics and crash reports are on by default. Turn them off with the "Anonymous usage analytics" switch in Settings › General or Settings › Privacy, or set `"analytics": { "enabled": false }` in `~/.atomic-agent-desktop/config.json`. The switch stops the app's own reporting at once, and the bundled agent stops after its next restart. If you already turned analytics off in the terminal agent and the desktop config does not set it, the app keeps it off. Message content, file paths, tool arguments, API keys and your IP address are never sent.

name: v0.6.6
body:
## Local model: recovers by itself

- A crashed local model server restarts automatically, and the reply in progress continues on the new server. A server that is alive but frozen is detected and restarted the same way. After three quick crashes it stops trying and tells you to run `/llm restart`.
- The chat now says why the agent went quiet: server crashed, restarting, back up, turn paused waiting for the model, answering again. The pause message names the real cause (connection refused or dropped, timeout, model loading, the actual HTTP code, the provider ending its reply with an error).
- A start only counts when our own server answers. A port taken by another program is detected: the agent takes over its own leftover server, stops an abandoned one, or moves to the next free port and saves it.
- Requests to the local server can no longer hang the agent. A frozen or silent server no longer blocks startup or the start of a turn.
- Switching to the local model while its server is already running now puts that server under the same watch, and it is stopped on quit.

## Models and vision

- Vision uses the model that is running right now: local, cloud, or a Fusion worker. It follows a model switch without a restart. A model that cannot read images is not offered the tool, and a direct call is refused with a clear message instead of an error loop.
- After a model switch, the agent is told which model it is running on, so an earlier "this model can't do it" no longer sticks.
- `/llm provider <id>` actually switches the provider. `/memory`, `/mcp` and `/model pull|use` with an unknown id no longer fail silently.
- Esc stops a cloud reply immediately, even when the provider has gone quiet, and closes the connection. A stopped turn ends as a cancellation instead of saving a half-written answer.
- Long pauses in a reply are no longer cut at 5 minutes.
- A reply that ends with a provider error is retried, not shown as the answer.

## Chat and sessions

- A message sent while the agent is working shows in the chat immediately.
- `[switch back]` on background-turn notices returns to that thread, including while its first reply is still running.
- A reply sent together with memory notes ends the turn, so the answer is not written several times.
- The session list loads 40 at a time and pages as you scroll. Empty `+ new` sessions no longer leave rows behind.
- Opt-in `sessions.retention` removes sessions and traces older than 90 days at startup.
- The composer and hint strip wrap on tall windows instead of cutting text.
- `/context`: "tasks per turn" goes up to 1000.

## Settings, integrations, MCP

- MCP: `R` restarts one server and `e` turns it on or off, also over HTTP (`POST /api/mcp/servers/{name}/restart|enable|disable`).
- Secret integration fields are masked while you type.
- `PATCH /api/config` merges into the file instead of wiping providers and MCP servers.
- Onboarding import runs straight from the ticks, with no preview screen. Enter imports from any row.
- `serve` exits when the process that started it is gone (`--no-parent-exit` keeps it running).
- The Local pane keys (`d g i x G U`) work again.
- On Windows, uninstall removes `atag.cmd` and the PATH entry.
- Also fixed: several config keys and help defaults, error-report grouping, and shutdown races that crashed on exit.

name: v0.6.4
body:
Twelve fixes. Ten of them are one bug wearing different hats, and two come from Fusion field logs.

## Tool results stop being cut at ingestion

`compressToolResult` was trimming tool output to 400 characters and 12 trailing lines **as it was stored**. The summary it returns *is* the `tool_result` turn, so whatever it dropped was gone — not deferred, not pageable. Twelve call sites took that bare default.

- **#477** — nine ordered listings (`git log/status/branch`, `github pr/issue list`, `proc.list`, `window.list`, `browser.tabs`, shell jobs) were cut to their *oldest* three to five rows with the header line gone. `git log` now returns 20 commits newest-first; `proc.list` keeps its `PID PPID USER CPU% MEM% COMMAND` header.
- **#470** — `os.shell.run` took the bare default while `git.diff` passed 64 KB, so the model could not read the end of a command it had just run. It now keeps the tail, and the wide budget is paid once on the step that consumes it rather than re-pasted into history.
- **#474** — `skill.run_script` dropped the `exit:` header first, so a script's success was invisible.
- **#475** — five MCP and vision sites discarded budgets their own code declared.
- **#473** — the loop veto was cut on the very sentence that tells the model what to do instead of repeating.
- **#472** — the forced reply quoted the no-progress streak and called it a refusal count.
- **#471** — the skills catalog truncated silently (17 of 33 skills on the reporter's install) and `skills.catalogTokenBudget` in `config.json` was parsed and ignored. Config version **70**.

## Memory

- **#469** — `memory_links` stayed empty on every multi-step turn: the allowlist was rebuilt after each tool batch and was empty by the time reflection read it. A skipped link generation now says why in the trace instead of being silent.
- **#468** — `memory.embeddings.enabled` was cleared by a transient daemon observation, permanently dropping hybrid recall to FTS5. The reconciler is one-way now: only a user action or a durable disk fact clears the opt-in.

## Fusion

- **#487** — a worker's 45-minute clock started before it had a server slot, while the first-token budget is 30 minutes by design. A four-task fan-out on a two-slot machine lost its tail to timeouts with zero tool calls. The clock now starts at the first token; `timeout` and `queued` are separate statuses from `max_steps`, because their remedies differ; a task can size its own `maxSteps` / `timeoutMs` up to 4× the configured default; and every row carries `queueWaitMs`, so a worker nothing ever answered is distinguishable from one that queued.
- **#488** — two workers implemented the same symbol with opposite field meanings and both satisfied the contract, which checks names. `provides[].shape` carries one line of meaning into the *consumer's* brief.

## Docs

- **#476** — 52 documented config defaults across 27 keys had drifted from the code, some by two orders of magnitude, with a guard test so they cannot drift again.

---

Verified against the built binary through a real terminal, not only in unit tests: listings, shell tails, skill-script output, the catalog marker, vision, MCP (including a 279-character resource URI round-tripping), the full veto text, memory links, and the embeddings latch measured side by side against v0.6.3 — where the flag flips to `false` within five seconds and here holds.

name: v0.6.3
body:
23 PRs on top of v0.6.2 — the harness release: Fusion and local models that finish the task, and tools that stop damaging the user's work.

### Fusion that delivers
- **Workers see the request.** Every brief quotes the operator's original request; briefs up to 32K chars; a worker's reads are confined to its working directory and the fan-out's write scope (#426).
- **Task status is ground truth, not the worker's reply.** A task that declared files and wrote nothing is `no_changes`; a reply on the forced final step is `max_steps`; the delegate result opens with a status table for every task and the call reports `all_ok` / `partial` / `all_failed` (#426, #428, #431).
- **A contract between the parts of a fan-out.** `fusion.delegate` takes `owners`, `provides`, `requires`, `inputs` and `checks`; parts run in waves ordered by `requires → provides`; one refusal names every problem at once (#431, #439, #459).
- **Check before you accept.** New read-only `verify.syntax` and `verify.run` (command, service or headless page) run against a throwaway copy of the working directory; contract checks run through them (#432).
- **No more wasted workers.** Worker time limits come from measured throughput; a worker is handed back only after it stalls, never mid-generation; reasoning effort and output caps reach the provider; `llm.runMode.fusion.cloudWorkers` caps a cloud fan-out; `/runmode status` says what will actually run (#434, #439).
- **A stalled review must act.** A Fusion orchestrator that keeps reading without delegating gets one notice, then can only `fusion.delegate` or `reply` (`llm.runMode.fusion.reviewStallSteps`, #459).

### Local models
- **The KV cache survives long turns.** Prompts only append between history cuts, sessions keep their llama-server slot across steps and resumes, context and fan-out width are sized from the GGUF header and a throughput probe, sliding-window models launch with `--swa-full` (#429, #436).
- **Bounded thinking.** `localModels.reasoningBudgetTokens` (default 1,500) caps the reasoning prelude before each tool call; `localModels.thinking: off` now applies to every prompt (#453).
- **Per-request grammar and tool roles.** A local orchestrator can no longer generate calls the gate would refuse; workers and orchestrators get their own tool sets (#430).
- Families without a hand-built profile render through llama-server's own chat template (`localModels.useServerTemplate`, #435).

### Cloud providers
- **Native multi-turn messages** for OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, AIMLAPI and Gemini, with Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints, cache-capable routes for Google models and cached tokens on the usage record (#433).
- Reasoning fields and tagged tool calls parsed for every OpenAI-compatible kind; `o*` / `gpt-5` models no longer get `temperature` / `max_tokens` (#433).
- Provider errors told apart: exhausted credit stops the turn resumably, retry hints are honoured up to 180 s, a context-length rejection learns the window, repacks and retries once (#435).

### Tools that protect your work
- **Your files are safe.** Replacing a pre-existing file saves the previous bytes and says so; `os.fs.restore` brings them back; a file the request names as an input is not replaced without `overwrite: true` (#438, #459).
- **Long shell commands detach instead of hanging.** After `tools.shell.defaultTimeoutMs` (10 min) the agent gets the output so far and a job id to `wait`, `kill` or keep (#452).
- **Reads outside the working directory ask first** through the approval ladder (`fs_read_outside`; `agent.readScope: unrestricted` to opt out) (#452).
- Calls carrying model control markers or unknown argument keys are refused with the expected keys; batched writes run whole under auto-approval; `.js`/`.json` writes are parse-checked; `os.fs.grep { literal: true }` (#427, #435, #438).
- A `reply` batched with work tools is a progress note, not the end of the turn (#453).
- Bigger defaults for today's contexts: 200 conversation pairs, 32K batch results, 8K render cap, 60 worker steps (#437).

### Also
- **Atomic Chat (local)** provider preset; an External llama.cpp URL on `:1337` opens the wizard on it (#424).
- **Re-run first-time setup** any time: `/onboarding` (alias `/setup`), the Setup menu row "Run first-time setup again…", or `atomic-agent tui --onboarding`. Providers, keys, models, sessions and memory are untouched, and backing out writes nothing (#425).
- Downvoted profile facts, pinned ones included, now leave `### profile` as `memory.voting.profileFilterThreshold` promised (#423).
- **Model downloads no longer hang at 9x%.** A connection the CDN throttles is swapped for a fresh one, and connections that finish their slice take over the rest of a slow one (#462).
- A message typed while a turn is running is labelled `YOU · steered into the running turn`, so the turn's answer is no longer read as its reply; `[try again]` on a stopped turn re-sends the turn's own request, not the steer (#461).
- The forced reply after a `wandering` loop stop says what actually happened instead of "a no-progress loop after 12 blocked attempts" (#460, refs #458).

Config migrates automatically to v69; values you set yourself are kept.

name: v0.6.1
body:
11 PRs (#411–#421) on top of v0.6.0 — a reliability release for hosted reasoning models and long-running personal agents.

### Hosted models no longer fail turns because of memory sub-calls
- **"Turn failed" on models whose endpoint refuses structured output is fixed.** The query rewriter shared the turn's fallback state, so one refused rewrite moved the next step onto the local link — with no local model running, the turn died with `fetch failed`. It now runs on its own partition (#411), and a sub-call whose endpoint refuses `response_format` is retried once without it (#417).
- **Memory timeouts sized for hosted reasoning models.** Reflection and link generation default to 60 s (was 10 s / 8 s); the query rewriter to 10 s and it runs once per turn instead of before every step (#415, #416). Existing configs that still carry the old defaults migrate automatically (config v65); values you set yourself are kept.
- **A timed-out memory sub-call now cancels its request** instead of leaving it running and billing (#412).
- **OpenAI strict mode and Qwen no longer reject memory sub-calls** (#414).
- **You are told when memory keeps failing:** one notice per session names the setting to change (#419).

### Clearer failures and routing
- When every provider in the fallback chain fails, the error names the primary's real refusal, not just the last link's `fetch failed` (#418).
- `providerPreferences` on an OpenRouter provider is now actually sent as OpenRouter's routing (`order`, `allow_fallbacks`, …) (#413).

### Channels and memory
- **Telegram reconnects by itself** after a non-fatal polling stop, on the same backoff as Discord; an invalid token or another process polling the same bot still stops it, now with the reason logged (#420, refs #409).
- **Pinned profile facts are never silently dropped from the prompt.** Pinned facts render first, the section is packed whole lines at a time, a clip raises a visible warning, and a new `memory.profile.maxEntries` (default 500) caps unpinned facts without ever evicting pinned ones (#421, fixes #407).

name: v0.6.0 — Fusion
body:
60 PRs (#347–#406) on top of v0.5.6.

## Fusion — one model plans, another builds

A run mode over two providers. One orchestrates: it reads, plans, briefs, and reviews what comes back. The other executes, several workers at once, each on its own throwaway session. Pick it in the composer (`ctrl+r`, or `/runmode fusion`).

- **Two slots, either kind.** Cloud plans while local builds, or local plans while cloud builds — the pairing is yours. The `⇄` between the two model names trades the seats in one click (`/runmode swap` from the keyboard).
- **The orchestrator does not build.** Every mutating tool is refused for its whole turn: read, delegate, reply, nothing else. Rework goes back out as another fan-out with what was wrong and what good looks like. Without this it read the workers' replies, decided it could do better, and rewrote their files — which is not orchestration, it is a very expensive single agent.
- **One approval per task.** `fusion.delegate` asks once, naming the task titles and the directory the fan-out will write in. Every worker in that turn then writes files and runs commands inside it — the build, the tests, the output — without asking again. Reach outside it and the call is refused, and comes back as a task to re-delegate.
- **The machine sizes the pool, the model sizes the fan-out.** Worker count is not a setting: the orchestrator knows how divisible the job is and asks for what it needs, bounded by the task count and the server's request slots. Slots are derived from the hardware, not typed in.
- **Live feed.** Each worker announces itself as it starts, picks up a tool, and lands, tagged with the model running it.

## The agent loop keeps going

- **A truncated completion is recovered, not fatal** (#359) — a reply the server cut short is retried with a larger cap or a re-packed prompt, once per step.
- **An unparseable tool call no longer ends the turn** (#387): the model is told what it emitted and what the schema wanted, and gets one repair.
- **An empty native-tools completion is retried** (#393) instead of being read as "the model is done".
- **Fallover within the provider class** (#386): a dead cloud link tries its siblings before falling to local, and a 402 repairs itself against the credit balance. The chat says when the primary drops out (#384, #385).
- **Output ceilings you choose** (#381, #382): cloud completions are no longer capped at the llama-server budget.

## Local models

- **Parallel range downloads** (#354) — 16 connections, resumable across an offline period and a relaunch (#356). A vision model pulls its GGUF and mmproj together (#353), and a projector that fails no longer strands the weights (#364).
- **Ping when it lands** (#360, #361): Telegram, Discord or e-mail when a background download finishes.
- **Restart the model server from the TUI** (#377), and `supportsTools: "strict"` is honoured on the tools payload (#395, #402).

## Git, GitHub and e-mail

- **Local repository writes** (#373): `init`, `add`, `commit`, `checkout`.
- **Remote sync, off by default** (#368, #372): `push`, `pull`, `fetch`, `clone` and `remote` are inert until you turn the switch on for that repository. A repository stays local unless you say otherwise.
- **GitHub in the hub** (#357): open PRs and file issues as yourself; `/report` files one with the session's logs at a privacy level you pick (#358).
- **The agent's own inbox** (#361, #362): `os.email.inbox` and `os.email.send`, with a verified owner address.

## Channels

- **A session per chat** (#347): every Telegram chat, forum topic and Discord channel keeps its own thread, and the Swarm tab runs several bots at once.
- **Attachments both ways** (#348–#352): files sent to the agent reach it, and files it produces come back as photos, documents or uploads.
- **More than one Discord owner** (#388), a `/model` command in both channels (#394), and the model is told who is speaking and where (#401).

## The TUI

- **No more blink** (#390, #379): Ink's incremental renderer lost the frame on a session swap and left the composer drawn over itself. Full-frame repaint, deliberately.
- **The session rail** — every session listed (#367), reorderable with Shift+↑/↓ or the mouse (#369), pinnable (#376), and imported transcripts render faithfully (#366, #370).
- **The outage readout ticks**, names the failure and keeps the route on screen (#380).

## Fixes

Images are typed by their bytes, not their file extension (#399) — a PNG renamed `.jpg` no longer dies on an opaque provider 400. A long session's trace keeps its end rather than its start (#397). Intraword asterisks survive Telegram (#392). Only the lock's owner may release it (#400).

## New config

`USER_CONFIG_VERSION` 51 → 64. Every block is additive; an existing file gains the behaviour and stays readable.

```jsonc
{
  "llm": {
    "runMode": {
      "mode": "fusion",
      "fusion": {
        "orchestratorProvider": "openrouter",
        "workerProvider": "local-llama",
        "workerMaxSteps": 40,
        "workerTimeoutMs": 2700000
      }
    }
  },
  "localModels": { "managed": { "parallel": 2 } }
}
```

## Upgrading

`atomic-agent update`, or download below. The local tool grammar changed in this release, so the first local prompt after upgrading rebuilds the KV cache and is slower than usual — once.

name: v0.5.6
body:
20 PRs (#326–#345) on top of v0.5.5.

## Integrations — Composio, Discord, and one place for credentials

- **Integrations hub** (#328): one tab where every third-party credential goes, rendered from a descriptor rather than a bespoke pane per service — and each integration carries its own numbered setup walkthrough on screen until it connects (#343).
- **Composio** (#327, #330): ~1500 SaaS toolkits over MCP, gated on the API key alone. Four meta-tools, so the prompt cost is flat regardless of catalogue size, and the model is told how to reach for them.
- **Discord remote control** (#331): DMs and @mentions reach the agent, replies come back, and approvals prompt in the channel the turn came from. Raw HTTP + Gateway — zero new dependencies — and `MESSAGE_CONTENT` is never requested, so the bot cannot read guild chatter it was not addressed in.
- **Telegram moved into the hub** (#329, #332): the Telegram tab is gone; `/telegram` still works and lands on the hub. A dead polling loop now reports itself instead of sitting on a green badge (#333), a failed channel says *why* (#337), and "already running in another atomic-agent" is no longer red (#338).
- Credentials saved in the hub now reach the **running** channel (#342) — before, a token pasted on a fresh install did nothing until the next launch.

## Downloads that survive

- **Resumable model downloads** (#334): `.part` + sidecar, `Range`/`If-Range` resume, retry with backoff, stall watchdog. A kill at 90% of a 20 GB GGUF no longer costs the whole transfer.
- **`models pull --background`** (#335): a detached worker that outlives the terminal, with `models downloads` / `cancel` / `clear`.
- **TUI pulls run through that worker** (#336): quit the app and the download keeps going; reopen and it is adopted, landed and activated.

## The agent loop

- **A turn is a task, not a step budget** (#344). `agent.maxSteps` (25) is now a checkpoint interval; what ends a task is `agent.task.maxSteps` (1000), `agent.task.maxDurationMs` (2 h), the model finishing, the loop breaker, or you. Every leg boundary reports itself (`» still working — 50 steps, 12 min (ceiling 1000)`), a leg where nothing usable came back ends the run, and the closing message names the ceiling and says `continue` picks up from there — instead of `(stopped: max_steps reached without a reply)`.
- **A provider outage is waited out, not fatal** (#345). The same step is retried on a 2s→30s backoff for up to five minutes, with a live readout in the composer and a sticky `provider unreachable` state once the budget is spent. A 404 from a wrong URL or a 401 from a dead key still fails instantly — a typo is not an outage.

## Reliability and diagnostics

- Reflection can no longer reject after a store closes (#326) — four live crash clusters.
- A dropped stream explains itself instead of printing `terminated` (#339).
- Model failures carry `tool_transport` / `failure_stage` tags (#340).
- Subscription CLIs (`claude`, `codex`) launch through `cmd.exe` on Windows (#341).

## New config keys

```jsonc
{
  "agent": {
    "maxSteps": 25,
    "task": { "maxSteps": 1000, "maxDurationMs": 7200000, "autoContinue": true },
    "providerWait": { "enabled": true, "maxWaitMs": 300000 }
  }
}
```

`USER_CONFIG_VERSION` 51 → 53. Both new blocks are additive: an existing config file gains the behaviour and stays readable. `agent.task.autoContinue: false` restores the previous "stop at `maxSteps`" behaviour, and `agent.providerWait.enabled: false` restores fail-fast on a transport error.

name: v0.5.5
body:
Sixteen fixes and features on top of v0.5.4 — reliability of the LLM path, a composer that tells you what it is doing, and per-session context.

## Stability

- **The TUI no longer dies of heap exhaustion after a long run.** `NODE_ENV` now defaults to `production` outside the SEA binary too, so the development React reconciler stops recording a `performance.measure()` per commit. An unattended agent used to go silent around the eleven-hour mark. (#310)
- **A streaming local generation is bounded by idle time, not total time.** `localModels.requestTimeoutMs` was a wall-clock deadline over the whole generation, so any honest answer longer than five minutes was killed mid-stream and its tokens discarded. (#323)
- **A stream that dies before its first chunk is retried.** A provider that accepts the connection, thinks for a long time and then drops the socket without emitting anything no longer fails the turn — even with no fallback provider configured. (#313)
- **Provider-availability failures fall over instead of blocking.** A llama-server 404/405 was filed as a "grammar" failure, and an uninstalled or logged-out subscription CLI as a "tool" failure; neither could advance the fallback chain. (#322)
- **Parallel tool calls stay apart on providers that send no `index`.** Streamed calls are keyed by id when the provider gives one, so two calls stop folding into one with their arguments spliced together. (#309, issue #103)
- **A cloud session stops probing the local llama backend.** No `/health` warnings, no 3-second footer poller and no local profile refresh for a backend the session never talks to. (#324, issue #112)

## Composer and context

- **A stop button in the composer while a turn runs** — and a stopped turn now says `Agent stopped by user.` with a `[try again]` action, instead of dressing your own stop as a provider failure. (#316)
- **A persistent update banner** in the top-right of the status bar: it survives skipping the startup modal, narrates the install, and its `Update` cell is clickable even while the modal is open. (#317)
- **The context readout counts the KV-cached prefix.** On a warm local cache the chip was showing only the tokens evaluated on the last request — which is why moving the task selector made the figure leap about fourfold. (#318)
- **The chip recalculates live** on task-selector moves and model switches, instead of waiting for the next prompt build. (#319)
- **Context occupancy and the provider/model are now per session**, stamped at the end of each turn and restored when you switch back — so reopening yesterday's thread shows its real gauge, and two projects on two models stop quietly sharing one. (#320, #321)

## Tools

- **A streaming native-tool contract probe at provider setup.** Reaching `/v1/models` proves nothing about a streamed completion carrying a `tools` payload; routes that pass the key check and then fail every real turn are now named at setup rather than by your first message. (#315, issue #110)
- **`read_document` routes source files to `os.fs.read`**, and its `format` argument is a closed set on every surface instead of an open string that invited unusable guesses. (#312)
- **The loop detector catches overlapping re-reads** of an unchanged file — shifted `offset`/`limit` on the same bytes no longer slips past argument hashing. (#314)

## What's Changed
* Release candidate 2026-09-03: PRs #309-#324 by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/325
* fix(llm): key streamed tool calls by id when the provider sends no index by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/309
* fix(cli): default NODE_ENV to production so the TUI stops leaking to OOM by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/310
* fix(install): say why an unpublished platform has no binary by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/311
* fix(tools): route source files from read_document to os.fs.read by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/312
* fix(openai): retry a stream that dies before its first chunk by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/313
* feat(loop-detector): detect overlapping re-reads of an unchanged file by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/314
* feat(providers): probe streaming native-tool contract at setup by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/315
* TUI: stop button in the composer while a turn is running by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/316
* TUI: persistent top-right update banner (+ --fake-update testing ground) by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/317
* fix: context readout collapses to the KV-cache delta, then jumps ~4x when the task selector moves by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/318
* feat: composer context chip recalculates live — task selector and model switches by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/319
* Persist the context gauge per session and restore it on switch by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/320
* Pin the provider/model to each session and restore it on switch by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/321

* fix(llm): a streaming llama response is bounded by idle time, not total time by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/323

name: v0.5.1
body:
Community feedback release: 18 fixes and features sourced from GitHub issues and the Discord server — every report from the last month triaged, fixed, and independently verified.

## Reasoning & providers
- **No more chain-of-thought leaking into replies** — unparseable reasoning is never "salvaged" as the agent's answer; prompts are now transport-aware, so native function-calling providers stop being ordered to emit text-JSON tool calls (#286, fixes #285)
- **Think-tag prefill no longer sent to native-tools chat providers** — stops Ollama Cloud silently corrupting literal `<think>` strings; live reasoning display survives grammar fallover (#287, fixes #283)
- **Live reasoning no longer freezes at the first `{` in the model's thoughts** — the stream parser only hands off to tool-call parsing on a real `{"tool": "` payload (#292)
- **Gemini `RetryInfo.retryDelay` honored on 429/503** — cooldowns from the error body instead of burning retries on fixed backoff (#271, fixes #106)
- **Final step reserved for a real answer** — the agent replies instead of stalling at `max_steps`; user cancellation is no longer mislabelled as `max_steps` (#272, fixes #107 — based on @mikemikimike's #269)

## Security & correctness
- **MCP tools with `trust: approval_gated` actually route through the approval gate** — strict `readOnlyHint === true` exempts; everything else fails closed (#273, fixes #132)
- **Search cache + provider cooldown persist across restarts** — per-task processes stop re-spending quota (#274, fixes #256)
- **`skills.catalogTokenBudget` is honored** — the skill catalog is no longer hard-capped at 4096 chars (#288)
- **Warn on repeated test runs against an unchanged workspace** (#276, fixes #118)

## Local models
- **CPU llama.cpp fallback** — iGPU-only Windows boxes get an automatic, visible fallback to the CPU build instead of a silent model-load failure; `backendVariant` config for manual control (#293)
- **Multi-GPU tensor split** — `localModels.managed.tensorSplit` passes `--split-mode layer --tensor-split` to the managed llama-server (#298)
- **Ollama steer** — pointing the External llama.cpp URL at an Ollama server now offers a one-key jump into the OpenAI-compatible provider wizard, prefilled (#290)

## TUI
- **Clicking a slash-command completion runs the clicked command**, not the half-typed buffer (#289)
- **Free/paid price filter** on both cloud model pickers — press `p` (#295)
- **Mouse-report hardening over ssh** — coordinate spam can't leak into the composer; a tripped session auto-disables mouse tracking with a `/mouse` hint (#297)
- **Legacy conhost guard** — Windows 10 cmd/PowerShell (outside Windows Terminal) reserves the bottom row to stop shaking/duplicated last-row rendering, with a one-time Windows Terminal hint; opt out with `ATOMIC_AGENT_CONHOST_GUARD=0` (#291)

## Memory
- **`memory export --vault <path>`** — one-way, idempotent Obsidian export of notes/lessons/procedures with frontmatter and wikilinks (#296)
- **MEMORY_GUIDE.md** — the memory system end to end, with worked examples (#294)

Thanks to everyone who reported on Discord and GitHub: l.hk, thegreatteacher, detraxsenpai, adithr, johnfasterlane_83003, magicw0rm5, gokcanakalin, yablokolabs, Ramyazzam, sosidudku1, and @mikemikimike for #269.

name: v0.5.0
body:
## The TUI answers the mouse, and the mouse answers back

Seven changes, all in the terminal UI, all about things you could see but not touch.

### Select text with a plain drag

Mouse support and native drag-to-select are mutually exclusive at the terminal level — while the app receives clicks, the terminal stops selecting. Now the drag itself resolves the conflict: drag across message text once and mouse reporting pauses for 10 seconds with a notice — drag again and native selection works, in every terminal, no modifier to remember. Shift- or Alt-modified presses open the same window instantly where terminals deliver them, and the idle strip carries a clickable `[drag] select text` chip that skips the first drag entirely. `/mouse off` remains the permanent form. (#278)

### Links you can actually open

- URLs in chat are OSC 8 hyperlinks everywhere now — including while the reply is still streaming, and including scheme-less `www.example.com`, which previously wasn't detected at all. (#277)
- Terminals that ignore OSC 8 (stock macOS Terminal.app among them) get a working path too: messages with URLs grow `[open <host>]` chips beside `[copy]`, routed through the app's own mouse layer — one click opens the OS default browser. Only http(s) is ever handed to the OS. (#277)

### The rail folds away

A `«` in the sidebar's top-right corner folds it; a `»` at the head of the status bar brings it back; `/sidebar` does both from the keyboard. The fold is your choice and survives resizes — the restore control only appears when the terminal could actually seat the rail again. (#275)

### Tasks catch up with Sessions

The Tasks header gets its own `+ new` chip, landing straight in the create form, with the `N running` counter seated mid-gap between title and chip. The counter also counts correctly now: it used to read at most "5 running" because it measured the five visible rows, not the task list. (#282)

### ⚠️ ctrl+p retires — the menu answers to Esc alone

Esc already opened the menu from an empty idle prompt and already closed every overlay; `ctrl+p` was a second name for the same thing. It is removed end to end — binding, hint chips, rail label, docs. Muscle memory: **Esc on an empty prompt**, the `☰ Menu` button, the breadcrumb, or the `ctrl+g` chords. (#280)

### Smaller

- The idle hint strip now advertises `ctrl+n · new window` — the shortcut existed, nothing on screen said so. The chip is clickable. (#279)
- New curated local model: **Qwen3.8 27B Uncensored** (`JonathanColetti/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GGUF`, noMTP Q4_K_M, 16.5 GB, vision projector included) — the most-downloaded uncensored upload on Hugging Face of the last month. Deliberately last in every list, tagged **Use at your own risk**, and never the auto-recommendation. (#281)

## What's Changed
* feat(tui): clickable links in every chat message, including mid-stream by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/277
* feat(models-catalog): add uncensored Qwen3.8 27B, pinned last and never auto-recommended by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/281
* feat(tui): a collapsible rail — « folds it, » brings it back, /sidebar for the keyboard by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/275
* feat(tui): + new on the Tasks header, with the running counter centered — and counted correctly by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/282
* feat(tui): the menu answers to esc alone, ctrl+p retires by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/280
* feat(tui): advertise the ctrl+n new-window key in the idle hint strip by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/279
* feat(tui): Shift+drag text selection while the mouse is on by @plombeer31 in https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/pull/278

name: v0.4.2
body:
## Steer context in tasks, not tokens

One task is a thing you asked plus everything the agent did answering it. `agent.conversationMaxPairs` (1–100, default 20) says how many the prompt carries, and the context panel now has a selector for it:

```
 context · 13.6k of 128k window · 11%
 prompt scaffold        5.9k   5% ==========
 conversation              6  <1%
 free                 106.2k  83%
────────────────────────────────────────────
 tasks per turn      −   20  +   sent each turn (1-100)
```

Every figure above the selector recalculates as you move it, so the cost of the choice is on screen while you make it. Click `−`/`+` or press `-`/`+`. This replaces the old `transcript` line, the `capped by …` sentence and the `set auto (a)` button.

Tokens remain the ceiling underneath — a task has no bounded size, so N tasks can still exceed a window, and whichever limit cuts more wins.

### ⚠️ Behaviour change

History is now capped at **20 tasks** by default, where previously only the 32k token cap applied. A long, cheap history that used to survive whole will be trimmed. Set `agent.conversationMaxPairs` to `100` to effectively turn it off:

```
atomic-agent config set agent.conversationMaxPairs 100
```

### Fixed

- **`set auto` could shrink the transcript 30×** — with no window known it fell back to `tokenBudget * 0.35` = 1050 tokens, taking the transcript from 32,000 to 1,050, the opposite of what it promised.
- **Cloud models had no context window at all** in the prompt budget — it came only from the llama-server `/props` probe, so no window clamp was ever applied off the local path. The model catalogue now reaches the budget.
- **`config set agent.approvalLevel` could never succeed** — the one safety-critical key rejected the value it had just been given.
- **`Retry-After` could corrupt a redirect URL** in `os.http.request`, turning a plain 429-with-redirect into a `blocked` result.
- **The approval prompt advertised keys that did nothing** — the hint strip said `y`/`n` while only `ctrl+y`/`ctrl+d` worked.
- **The uninstall dialog did not hold the keyboard** — the confirmation word landed in the composer behind it, and Esc opened the operator menu on its way out.
- **Plan mode**: the composer hint could never render, and the plan buttons were mouse-only. They answer to `ctrl+y` / `ctrl+b` / `ctrl+d` now.

### Reliability

A dead socket is a transport failure rather than a tool bug (#262) · a closed pipe or vanished tty no longer crashes the agent (#263) · an empty completion gets one repair before the turn dies (#264) · errno survives being rewrapped (#265) · stacks Sentry can actually read (#266).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent/compare/v0.4.1...v0.4.2
